findings.title: Float precision causes incorrect price storage
findings.description: All three ingestion paths convert prices to minor units using `int(parse_amount(...) * minor_unit_factor(...))`. Due to IEEE 754 floating-point representation, this truncates instead of rounding: `int(19.99 * 100) = 1998` instead of 1999. Verified: '19,99 EUR' stores as 1998, '17.99 GBP' as 1798, '0.29 EUR' as 28. This violates REQ-1 which requires exact conversion. Fix by using `round()` before `int()`, or use Decimal arithmetic in parse_amount.

findings.title: INSERT OR REPLACE deletes price history
findings.description: upsert_listing uses `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO listings` which deletes the old row before inserting the new one. The price_history table has `ON DELETE CASCADE` on listing_id, so all historical price entries are deleted. Verified: three upserts with prices 100, 200, 300 EUR result in only one price_history entry (the final 30000). This violates REQ-2 which states price history entries are never lost except by explicit delete. The code should use `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` like bulk.py does, which preserves the row and its history.
